title.en: Enhancing Presentations with Slides and Other Visuals
title.ms: Menambah Baik Pembentangan dengan Slaid dan Visual Lain

en: Explain the role of visuals in business presentations and list the types commonly used
Explain the difference between structured and free-form slides and when each is appropriate
Outline decisions in using a key visual and selecting colour, artwork and typefaces
Explain how to create effective slide content
Explain the role of navigation slides, support slides and handouts
ms: Terangkan peranan visual dalam pembentangan perniagaan dan senaraikan jenis yang lazim
Terangkan beza slaid berstruktur dan bentuk bebas serta bila setiap satu sesuai
Gariskan keputusan menggunakan visual utama serta memilih warna, seni grafik dan jenis taip
Terangkan cara mencipta kandungan slaid berkesan
Terangkan peranan slaid navigasi, slaid sokongan dan edaran (handout)

en: Visuals create interest, illustrate points hard to explain in words, add variety, and help audiences absorb and remember information. Research: learning can improve by up to **400%** because humans process visuals **60,000 times faster** than text.
The purpose of visuals is to **support** your spoken message, **not replace** it.
ms: Visual mencipta minat, menerangkan perkara sukar, menambah kepelbagaian dan membantu ingatan. Kajian: pembelajaran boleh meningkat **400%** kerana visual diproses **60,000 kali lebih pantas**.
Tujuan visual ialah **menyokong** mesej lisan, **bukan menggantikan**.

en: Prezis — Nonlinear; flexible structure and access, can include video and media, dynamic look.
Slides — (PowerPoint): easy to create, edit and customise, easy for online meetings; disadvantage is **linear** flow (harder to jump).
Overhead transparencies — Old school; need only a marker, no latest equipment, can write on them, never malfunction; limited to static displays.
Chalkboards and whiteboards — Record points in small groups; digital whiteboards can print, save and share.
Flip charts — Dependable low-tech; “group memory” in brainstorming.
Other visuals — E.g. a video of a focus group or a product sample can have more impact than text slides.
ms: Prezi — Tidak linear; fleksibel, boleh masuk video, dinamik.
Slaid — Mudah dicipta dan disunting; kelemahan aliran **linear**.
Overhead transparency — Lama; hanya perlu pen; terhad kepada paparan statik.
Papan hitam dan papan putih — Rekod perkara kumpulan kecil.
Carta selak (flip chart) — “memori kumpulan” semasa sumbang saran.
Visual lain — Video kumpulan fokus atau sampel produk.

en: Check presentation style — Match style to subject, audience and setting; check **cultural assumptions** (colours with negative connotations, too playful vs too serious).
Keep it simple — Faster to create, reduces distraction and misinterpretation, fewer things to go wrong.
Use your time wisely — Decide up front how much design is enough, stop there and use the time saved to **rehearse**.
ms: Semak gaya pembentangan — Padankan gaya; semak **andaian budaya** (warna bermakna negatif).
Pastikan ringkas — Lebih cepat, kurang gangguan, kurang risiko.
Guna masa dengan bijak — Tentukan tahap reka bentuk dan gunakan masa untuk **latihan**.

en: Discerning audiences are not fooled by visual razzle-dazzle; a shaky analysis won’t be saved by an over-the-top production. Ask how each visual helps the audience.
ms: Audiens bijak tidak terpedaya dengan visual berlebihan.

en: **Structured slides** follow the same basic format throughout and are based on templates with lots of bullet points; **free-form slides** are looser and favoured by many presentation specialists (Figure 17.2).
Advantages: **easy and fast to create** (choose scheme, template, type). Practical for routine presentations such as status updates, or when you are in a schedule crunch.

They can pack more information per slide, so they can be more effective for **complex ideas or interrelated data**, e.g. executives deciding budget cuts across eight divisions need a single comparison slide. Best solution: high-level summary slides supported by a detailed **handout**.
Disadvantage: the **mind-numbing** effect of dense, text-heavy slides that all look alike.
ms: **Slaid berstruktur** ikut format sama dan banyak bullet; **slaid bebas** lebih longgar.
Kelebihan: **mudah dan pantas**; sesuai untuk pembentangan rutin.
Boleh memuatkan lebih maklumat untuk **idea kompleks**; penyelesaian terbaik: slaid ringkasan + **handout** terperinci.
Kelemahan: kesan **membosankan** slaid padat teks yang serupa.

blocks.en: Slide 8 lists “Complex Ideas” and “Audience Response” in the advantages/disadvantages columns without explicit mapping. The mapping above follows reading order. Free-form slides are not described in the slide text; Extra (not in slides): free-form slides use a key visual and less text, and suit presentations where you want a stronger audience connection. Check your textbook.
blocks.ms: Slaid 8 menyenaraikan “Complex Ideas” dan “Audience Response” dalam lajur kelebihan/kekurangan tanpa pemetaan jelas. Pemetaan di atas ikut susunan bacaan. Slaid bentuk bebas tidak diterangkan dalam teks slaid; Extra (bukan dalam slaid): slaid bentuk bebas guna visual utama dan kurang teks, sesuai bila mahu hubungan audiens lebih kuat. Semak buku teks.

groups.ms: Kenapa reka bentuk slaid tidak berkesan
Visual utama, warna, grafik, taip muka

en: **“Death by PowerPoint”** describes the agony of dull, slide-heavy presentations. The problem is not the software; it is a tool that can be used well or poorly.
ms: **“Death by PowerPoint”** = pembentangan membosankan. Masalah bukan perisian.

blocks.ms: Kenapa reka bentuk slaid tidak berkesan

en: Slideument hybrids — Slide sets treated as standalone documents; too much information to be good visuals and too little to be good reports. Ideal: effective slides **plus a separate handout**; alternative: speaking notes in the notes field; if forced, more simple slides are better than fewer jam-packed ones.
ms: Slideument hybrid — Slaid dianggap dokumen; terlalu banyak untuk visual dan terlalu sedikit untuk laporan. Ideal: slaid + **handout berasingan**; lebih banyak slaid ringkas lebih baik.

en: Colour — Is far more than decoration: grabs attention, emphasises, creates contrast, isolates elements and sends nonverbal messages (elegance, sophistication, prudence). Cool grays/blues say something different from warm oranges or hot pink/lime.
Artwork — Two layers, **background** (like paper, stays the same) and **foreground** (unique content). The background must not compete with the foreground.

Typefaces and type styles — Avoid script/decorative; serif with care and only larger text; one or two per slide; bold for thin typefaces; avoid italics and ALL CAPS; extra white space between lines; be consistent.
ms: Warna — Menarik perhatian, menekankan, kontras dan menghantar mesej bukan lisan.
Seni grafik — Dua lapisan, **latar** dan **hadapan**; latar tidak boleh bersaing.
Jenis taip dan gaya taip — Elak skrip/hiasan; serif untuk teks besar sahaja; satu atau dua; elak italik dan HURUF BESAR; konsisten.

en: Slide masters — Use the **slide master** (colours, fonts, design elements apply to every slide) and **predefined layouts** (bulleted lists, charts in predictable places). Even switching from one to two columns can confuse readers.
ms: Slide master — Guna **slide master** dan **layout pratetap**.

blocks.en: Slideument = a hybrid of slide and document: too much text for a slide.
blocks.ms: Slideument = hibrid slaid dan dokumen: terlalu banyak teks untuk slaid.
Visual utama, warna, grafik, taip muka

en: **Key visual**: structure slides around a visual that organises and explains (pyramid = hierarchy; circular flow = process loops back) (Figure 17.3).
ms: **Visual utama**: piramid = hierarki; aliran bulat = proses berulang.

en: Audiences assign meaning to visual elements from the first slide; don’t force them to re-interpret with arbitrary changes.
ms: Audiens beri makna pada elemen sejak slaid pertama; jangan tukar sewenang-wenangnya.

en: Limit each slide to one thought, concept or idea
Write short bulleted phrases rather than long sentences
Use sentences only for quotations or the like
Phrase list items in parallel grammatical form
ms: Hadkan setiap slaid kepada satu fikiran
Tulis frasa pendek berpoin, bukan ayat panjang
Guna ayat hanya untuk petikan dan sebagainya
Frasakan item senarai dalam bentuk tatabahasa selari

en: Effects must support your message. Four categories
Watch for **information overload**: too much content (text and/or visuals) means viewers can’t process it and tune out. Pace information so people connect ideas from slide to slide.

Overstuffing slides overloads the audience, takes attention from the speaker, and forces smaller type. Slide text is like **headings and subheadings**: you want the audience to **listen, not read**; provide details in handouts.

Guidelines: one idea per slide; 4–5 lines with 4–5 words per line; avoid many text-heavy slides in a row; short bulleted phrases; sentences only for quotations; parallel form; active voice; short informative titles; let visuals carry the bulk (the more a visual conveys, the less text needed).
ms: Awas **beban maklumat**: terlalu banyak kandungan, penonton berhenti memproses.
Slaid terlalu padat membebankan audiens dan mengalih perhatian. Teks slaid ibarat **tajuk**: audiens **mendengar, bukan membaca**.
Garis panduan: satu idea; 4–5 baris, 4–5 patah; frasa pendek; selari; ayat aktif; tajuk pendek; visual bawa bahagian utama.

en: Limit each slide to **one thought, concept or idea**
Limit text to **four or five lines with four or five words per line**
Don’t show a large number of text-heavy slides in a row
Write short bulleted phrases rather than long sentences
Use sentences only for quotations or the like
Phrase list items in **parallel** grammatical form
Use visuals to convey the bulk of the information
ms: Hadkan setiap slaid kepada **satu fikiran, konsep atau idea**
Hadkan teks kepada **empat atau lima baris dengan empat atau lima perkataan setiap baris**
Jangan tunjuk banyak slaid padat teks berturut-turut
Tulis frasa pendek berpoin, bukan ayat panjang
Guna ayat hanya untuk petikan dan sebagainya
Frasakan item senarai dalam bentuk tatabahasa **selari**
Guna visual untuk menyampaikan sebahagian besar maklumat

en: Reduce the detail — Split across slides; give detail in handouts.
Simplify — E.g. use “Week of” once; remove the vertical scale and show values above bars.
Limit data — Line charts busy with more than 2–3 lines; bar charts crowded with more than 5–6 bars; tables with too many rows/columns.
Highlight key points — With arrows, bold and colour; one clear title (“Earnings up by 15%”).
Adjust size and design — White space, contrasting colours, clear label typeface.
ms: Hadkan data — Carta garisan >2–3 garisan sibuk; carta bar >5–6 sesak.
Serlahkan poin utama — ; satu tajuk jelas.
Laras saiz dan reka bentuk — **Laras saiz dan reka bentuk**.

blocks.en: Rule of thumb: 4-5 lines × 4-5 words, one idea per slide.
blocks.ms: Petua: 4-5 baris × 4-5 perkataan, satu idea setiap slaid.

blocks.en: Audiences view from across the room, so these must be simpler than print visuals.
blocks.ms: Audiens melihat dari jauh, justeru perlu lebih ringkas.

en: Effects must support your message. Four categories: **functional animation** (each must have a purpose), **transitions and builds** (builds, which control release of elements on a slide, are more useful than transitions), **hyperlinks / action buttons** (jump to a slide, website or program), **multimedia** (audio/video clips).
**Mobile**: broadcast slides to audience tablets and smartphones; can eliminate the projection system and reach remote viewers; each new slide is sent to subscribers.
ms: **Mudah alih**: siarkan slaid ke tablet/telefon; boleh tiada projektor; slaid dihantar kepada pelanggan.

en: Handouts are part of your presentation strategy

blocks.en: Apply the same quality control to slides as to any message: content, style, tone, readability, clarity and conciseness.
blocks.ms: Guna kawalan kualiti sama seperti mana-mana mesej.

en: **Slide sorter view**: add, delete, reposition slides, check consistency and effects, review story flow.
ms: **Slide sorter**: tambah, buang, susun semula, semak keseragaman dan aliran.

en: Readable — Text readable from the back of the room, stands out from background.
Simple — Can any slide be eliminated?
Clear — Main point grasped in a few seconds.
Concise and grammatically correct — ; parallel bullets.
Focused — One idea per slide; arrows/symbols draw attention.
Fully operational — Verify every slide, animation and effect.
ms: Ringkas dan tatabahasa betul — **Ringkas dan betul tatabahasa**.

en: Title slides: create a **first impression** — = cover page: title (and subtitle), your name, department (internal) or company (external), date, graphic. Two title slides are possible (topic; then affiliation and speaker credentials).
Agenda and program details: **communicate the agenda** — Agenda plus logistics (breaks, lunch, wireless password) to prevent later disruption.

Navigation slides: **guide the audience through your outline** — (based on your outline; most useful in long presentations): repeat the slide after each section showing what is covered and what is next (a **moving blueprint**); reuse in the close to review. Alternative: a simple **bumper slide** at each section break.
ms: Slaid tajuk: cipta **kesan pertama** — Tajuk, nama, jabatan/syarikat, tarikh, grafik; boleh dua slaid.
Agenda dan butiran program: **sampaikan agenda** — Agenda dan logistik.
Slaid navigasi: **bimbing audiens melalui rangka anda** — Ulang selepas setiap bahagian (**moving blueprint**); pilihan lain **bumper slide**.

en: Timing — Handing out slides before you start lets people take notes, but is risky with the **indirect approach** because they can read ahead to conclusions. Others describe handouts early but distribute them after speaking.
ms: Masa — Beri sebelum bermula membolehkan nota, tetapi berisiko dengan **pendekatan tidak langsung**; ada yang edar selepas bercakap.

en: Handouts are part of your presentation strategy, planned with slides. The presentation paints the big picture, connects ideas, sets emotional tone and rouses to action; handouts carry supporting detail at the audience’s own pace.

Good content: complex charts and diagrams, articles and technical papers, case studies, recommended resources (URL plus one or two sentences), copies of slides (with speaker comments and blank lines for notes).
ms: Handout sebahagian strategi; pembentangan beri gambaran besar, handout beri butiran sokongan.
Kandungan baik: carta kompleks, artikel, kajian kes, sumber disyorkan, salinan slaid.
